questions.question:
Part 1 – Interview
The examiner asks you some questions about yourself. Answer each question and give some extra information.

Do you like spending time outdoors? Why or why not?
Where do you go when you want to be in nature?
What did you do the last time you went to the countryside or the beach?
Which season do you like best? Why?
Would you like to go camping? Why or why not?
questions.explanation:
Give full answers: answer the question, then add a reason or an example. Use the past simple for the question about the last time you went somewhere, and would for the question about camping.

Model answers:
Yes, I love it. After a day at school I need some fresh air, so I often go for a walk or ride my bike.
There’s a big forest about twenty minutes from my town. My family goes there at weekends to walk and have picnics.
Last summer I went to the beach with my cousins. We swam in the sea and played volleyball on the sand all afternoon.
I like autumn best, because the trees turn red and orange and it isn’t too hot to go hiking.
I’d love to try it, but only in summer! I think it would be exciting to sleep under the stars.

questions.question:
Part 2 – Photo description
Look at the photograph. It shows four young people collecting rubbish on a sandy beach. They are all wearing gloves, and two of them are holding large black bags. One of them is picking up a plastic bottle from the sand. Next to them there are some more bags full of rubbish. Behind them you can see the sea and some rocks, and the sky is blue. Tell us what you can see in the photograph.

Talk for about one minute.
questions.explanation:
Describe the place, the people and what they are doing, using the present continuous (are collecting, is picking up). Say where things are (next to them, behind them). If you do not know a word, explain it in other words. Only describe what is in the photo; you can say what you think about it, but do not invent new details.

Model answer:
This photo was taken on a sandy beach. I can see four young people, and they’re collecting rubbish. They’re all wearing gloves to protect their hands. Two of them are holding large black bags, and one of them is picking up a plastic bottle from the sand. Next to them there are some more bags, and they’re full of rubbish, so I think they’ve been working for a while. Behind them I can see the sea and some rocks, and the sky is blue, so the weather looks nice. I think what they’re doing is really useful for the beach.

questions.question:
Part 3 – Collaborative task
A school wants to do more to help the environment. Here are some ideas the students are thinking about.

recycling bins in every classroom
a vegetable garden in the school grounds
a week when everyone walks or cycles to school
turning off lights and computers at lunchtime
a sale of second-hand uniforms and books
solar panels on the school roof

Talk together about how each idea could help the environment. Then decide which idea the school should try first.

Talk together for about two or three minutes.
questions.explanation:
Discuss the ideas one by one and give reasons for your opinions. Ask your partner what they think, agree and disagree politely, and try to make a decision together at the end. Useful language: How about …? I’m not sure that … would work. That’s a good idea because … Let’s go for …

Model conversation (part):
A: Let’s start with the recycling bins. They’re cheap and easy to put in every classroom.
B: That’s true, but many schools already have them. What do you think about the solar panels?
A: They’d save a lot of energy, but they’re very expensive. I don’t think the school can pay for them.
B: Good point. The vegetable garden is nice too, because students learn where food comes from.
A: Yes, but it needs a lot of work, and who looks after it in the holidays?
B: Hmm. So maybe the walking and cycling week? Everyone can join in, and it costs nothing.
A: I agree. Let’s choose that one first.

questions.question:
Part 4 – General conversation
The examiner asks you and your partner some questions about recycling and protecting nature. Give your opinion and talk to your partner too.

What do you and your family recycle at home?
Do you think people throw away too many things? Why?
What can young people do to protect nature?
Is it better to buy new things or second-hand things? Why?
Have you ever taken part in an activity to help the environment?
questions.explanation:
Give your opinion with a reason or an example, and respond to your partner (I see what you mean, but …; Me too!). Use the present perfect with ever for the last question.

Model answers:
We recycle paper, glass and plastic. We have three different bins in the kitchen, and my brother takes them out every Thursday.
Yes, definitely. People often buy new phones or clothes when the old ones still work perfectly well.
They can use less plastic, walk or cycle instead of asking for a lift, and tell their friends why it’s important.
It depends. For clothes and books, second-hand is great because it’s cheaper and better for the planet. But I’d buy some things new, like shoes.
Yes, once. Our class planted trees in a park near our school. It was hard work, but I felt really proud.
